resps:
elara thorne
glass artist, sculptor, and studio coordinator
42 magill road, norwood, south australia 5067
elara.thorne.glass@protonmail.com | 0412 345 678 | www.elarathorneglass.com.au | instagram: @elarathorneglass

professional summary
accomplished and technically proficient glass artist with over fifteen years of dedicated, full-time practice in hot glass, kiln-formed glass, and sophisticated coldworking techniques, currently based in adelaide, south australia. my interdisciplinary practice is recognized nationally and internationally for creating large-scale sculptural installations and intimate vessel-based works that rigorously investigate the intersection of natural phenomena, personal and collective memory, and the ecological fragility of water systems within the australian context. working from my studio in the adelaide foothills, i maintain a practice that intentionally spans functional studio glass, highly conceptual art installations, and collaborative public artworks throughout metropolitan adelaide and regional south australia. i possess extensive, hard-won technical expertise in traditional furnace glassblowing, delicate pâte de verre, technically demanding lost wax casting, precise flameworking, and complex multi-element kiln casting requiring advanced mold engineering. my work has been enthusiastically acquired by the art gallery of south australia, the national gallery of victoria, the corning museum of glass in new york, and numerous significant private collections across the asia-pacific region and north america. i am deeply committed to advancing the contemporary glass movement through rigorous studio experimentation, meaningful community engagement, and the generous mentorship of emerging artists within adelaide's vibrant and closely-knit arts ecology. i am currently seeking opportunities to contribute technically sophisticated and conceptually rigorous glass works to major exhibitions, ambitious public art commissions, and international biennales while continuing to expand the absolute boundaries of material possibility within this ancient yet continually evolving luminous medium.

technical specializations and core competencies
furnace glassblowing and hot sculpting including large-scale team blowing, advanced kiln forming techniques encompassing slumping, draping, and drop-out molds, investment mold making for lost wax and sand casting processes, pâte de verre and vitreous enameling on multiple substrates, intensive coldworking including grinding, polishing, and sandblasting, precision latheworking for functional vessels, neon and plasma tube fabrication and bending, scientific and artistic flameworking using borosilicate and soft glass, programmable kiln management and annealing cycle development, comprehensive studio management and furnace equipment maintenance including crucible replacement and burner calibration, conceptual development and logistical fabrication of large-scale multi-element installations, community arts facilitation and workshop instruction, persuasive grant writing and arts project management, digital rendering and three-dimensional modeling for glass-specific forms, professional photography and archival documentation of translucent and reflective materials, exhibition installation and theatrical lighting design optimized for glass-specific presentation contexts, health and safety compliance for silica dust and heavy metal exposure.

professional experience

lead artist and studio coordinator
adelaide hot glass studio / contemporary craft sa, stepney, south australia
march 2018 – present
responsible for the daily operational management of a thriving three-pillar hot glass studio environment serving twelve core resident artists, numerous casual studio renters, and a steady stream of corporate clients seeking team-building experiences. i coordinate the complex glassblowing schedule, meticulously maintain the two-hundred-and-fifty-pound capacity furnace and two glory hole systems, and oversee all annealing programs within four digital kilns to ensure optimal thermal management for pieces ranging from delicate drinking glasses to monumental sculptural forms weighing up to eighty kilograms and measuring over one meter in height. i lead, train, and mentor a rotating team of four studio assistants in preparing color bar, custom frit blends, and specialized cullet mixtures while enforcing rigorous occupational health and safety protocols consistent with work safe south australia guidelines. my independent creative output during this residency period has included the critically acclaimed "saline memory" series, comprising seven large-scale kiln-cast wall panels exploring the intricate desiccation patterns and salt crystalline structures observed at lake eyre in the state's far north. i also conceived and am currently fabricating the ongoing "antipodean translucence" commission for the adelaide airport terminal expansion, involving a suspended canopy of three hundred individually blown and coldworked glass elements. i regularly design and teach advanced glassblowing workshops and intensive masterclasses in coldworking, surface treatment, and mold making, attracting dedicated participants from across australia, new zealand, and singapore. additionally, i manage detailed client consultations for bespoke architectural lighting installations and custom interior glass elements, liaising directly with interior designers, landscape architects, and heritage consultants throughout south australia and western victoria.

senior studio technician
jamfactory, adelaide, south australia
june 2014 – february 2018
served as the senior technician within jamfactory's internationally renowned glass studio, supporting the creative practices of six associate artists, two trainees, and numerous visiting international artists-in-residence from europe, asia, and north america. my daily duties included raw batch mixing using proprietary silica formulas, careful furnace charging and thermal monitoring, daily pulling of murrine and complex colored cane, and the preventative maintenance of three front-loading electric kilns and one large-scale custom annealing chamber. i assisted in the physically demanding realization of complex multi-part works requiring precise timing, clear communication, and seamless coordination between the hot shop floor and the cold shop finishing area. during my four-year tenure, i collaborated closely with artists from sweden, japan, the czech republic, and the united kingdom, facilitating vital cross-cultural technical exchanges that substantially enriched the studio's pedagogical environment and expanded my own technical vocabulary. i developed and refined a proprietary studio method for embedding local mallee ash and south australian beach sand into blown vessel forms, creating a distinctive, crackled surface texture that directly references the state's arid agricultural landscapes and coastal ecosystems. i also proudly represented jamfactory at the australian glass art fair in sydney for three consecutive years, presenting technically demanding live demonstrations to captivated audiences frequently exceeding two hundred visitors per session, and contributing to the organization's significant annual sales revenue.

glassblowing apprentice and studio assistant
denison glass works, richmond, victoria
january 2010 – may 2014
completed a comprehensive and transformative four-year apprenticeship under the exacting guidance of master glassblower marcus denison, learning traditional venetian goblet-making techniques alongside bold contemporary sculptural approaches and production studio methods. i began by performing foundational but essential tasks such as gathering molten glass from the crucible furnace, marvering on the steel bench, and assisting with basic blown forms before progressively advancing to independent production of decanters, bowls, and sculptural objects suitable for gallery representation. i systematically mastered the use of the bench, jacks, diamond shears, and various hand tools while developing an intuitive, almost unconscious understanding of thermal rhythm, heat base, and gravity's constant role in successful form-making. i participated actively in the production of major architectural commissions for luxury melbourne hotels and private residences, including multiple cascading chandelier assemblies requiring hundreds of individually blown and precisely matched elements. this intensely formative period instilled in me a profound, lasting respect for teamwork, physical stamina, attention to minute detail, and the considerable demands of maintaining a sustainable, ethically grounded hot glass practice in a contemporary art market.

education

master of visual art (by research)
university of south australia, adelaide, south australia
completed 2016
thesis title: "evaporative topographies: representing hydrological memory through kiln-formed glass in post-drought south australia." this research rigorously investigated how glass materiality—specifically its unique capacity to hold, refract, transmit, and absorb light—could function as a potent metaphor for water scarcity, agricultural resilience, and environmental grief in the murray-darling basin. the accompanying major exhibition featured twelve kiln-cast sculptural forms, an immersive floor installation of slumped optical glass panels, and a suite of wall-mounted vitreous enamel drawings on float glass.

bachelor of visual arts (honours, first class)
university of south australia, adelaide, south australia
graduated 2013
major: glass, with complementary minors in printmaking and critical art theory. awarded the university medal for outstanding academic achievement in studio practice.

diploma of glass and design
adelaide college of the arts, adelaide, south australia
graduated 2009
comprehensive technical training in furnace operations, coldworking, kiln-formed glass, and professional studio etiquette.

selected exhibitions

2023 "littoral drift," solo exhibition, hugo michell gallery, adelaide. featured twelve new works examining coastal erosion along the fleurieu peninsula.
2022 "glassica," group exhibition, central museum of glass, hsinchu, taiwan.
2021 "common wealth: contemporary australian glass," group exhibition, national art school gallery, sydney.
2020 "saline geometries," solo exhibition, glass artist gallery, melbourne.
2019 "adelaide biennial of australian art: monsters and borders," art gallery of south australia, adelaide.
2018 "pacific rim glass," group exhibition, tacoma museum of glass, tacoma, washington, usa.
2016 "evaporative topographies," thesis exhibition, samstag museum of art, adelaide.
2014 "emerging makers," craft victoria, melbourne.

artist residencies

2022 creative residency, pilchuck glass school, stanwood, washington, usa. developed a new body of experimental work exploring marine bioluminescence using phosphorescent glass compounds and integrated led technology.
2017 visiting artist residency, australian national university, school of art and design, canberra. collaborated with the electronics department to create responsive glass installations activated by viewer proximity and ambient sound.
2015 regional residency, sturt gallery and studios, mittagong, new south wales. investigated the incorporation of local river silica sands into traditional pâte de verre crystalline mixtures.

awards and grants

2023 south australian government arts grant, twenty-five thousand dollars, for the research and development of a major public artwork at glenelg foreshore.
2021 woollahra small sculpture prize, highly commended, for "salt fracture vii."
2019 rakow commission, corning museum of glass, corning, new york, usa.
2017 helen lempriere traveling art scholarship, forty thousand dollars, for extended research into czech and swedish studio glass traditions.
2015 brown council emerging artist award, art gallery of south australia, including acquisition prize.

public and private collections

art gallery of south australia, adelaide.
national gallery of victoria, melbourne.
corning museum of glass, corning, new york, usa.
central museum of glass, hsinchu, taiwan.
university of south australia art collection, adelaide.
alexander and sylvia kole collection, perth.
numerous significant private collections throughout australia, japan, the united kingdom, and the united states.

media and publications

2023 "casting light: elara thorne's hydrological poetics," feature article by dr. fiona weston, craft arts international, issue 105, pages 34-41.
2021 "the new wave of australian studio glass," extended feature interview, studio glass magazine, volume 18, pages 12-19.
2019 artist profile and studio visit, abc radio national, "the art show" hosted by eddie waterson.
2017 "salt, sand, and silica," exhibition review, artlink magazine, volume 37, number 2.

professional affiliations and community service

professional member, australian glass art guild (agag), 2014–present.
elected board member, contemporary art society of south australia, 2020–present.
peer assessor, arts south australia, visual arts and craft funding rounds, 2021–present.
volunteer mentor, prince's trust australia, creative industries program, 2019–present.

references available upon request.

doc.prompt: A filmmaker is trying to get financing for a film about the history of the Internet. Write an essay to be used in the proposal to potential investors. The essay should be at least 50 sentences long.

arg_0: [{"role": "user", "content": "A filmmaker is trying to get financing for a film about the history of the Internet. Write an essay to be used in the proposal to potential investors. The essay should be at least 50 sentences long.", "type": "text"}]

resps:
The Internet is arguably the most transformative invention in human history, yet its origin story remains shockingly unknown to the billions who use it every single day. We check our phones before sleep and upon waking, conduct our commerce, confess our secrets, and forge our identities through a vast digital architecture that very few truly understand. A comprehensive cinematic history of the Internet is not merely an educational exercise; it is an urgent excavation of the invisible forces shaping modern civilization. This proposed documentary will trace the Internet’s lineage from a Cold War defense project to the all-encompassing global nervous system that defines the twenty-first century. Our film will reveal that behind every protocol, server, and line of code lies a deeply human story filled with ambition, idealism, rivalry, and unintended consequences.

The narrative begins in the paranoid shadow of the Cold War, when the Soviet launch of Sputnik catalyzed an unprecedented American investment in scientific research. From this anxiety emerged ARPA, the Advanced Research Projects Agency, and a radical idea that computers could be linked together to share information across vast distances. Visionaries like J.C.R. Licklider imagined a future where machines would connect minds in a global network, a concept he called the “Intergalactic Computer Network.” His dream was not about technology for its own sake, but about augmenting human intellect and fostering collaboration on a scale never before possible. In the late 1960s, engineers at UCLA and Stanford sent the first message over ARPANET, crashing the system after only two letters but birthing a revolution nonetheless. That fragile first connection, born in academic basements and government labs, would eventually evolve into a decentralized web immune to single points of failure. The filmmakers will spotlight the unsung architects of this early era, including Bob Taylor, who secured funding, and Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn, who designed the TCP/IP protocols. Their work was driven by an ethos of open exchange, a belief that knowledge belonged to everyone and that barriers between disciplines and institutions should dissolve.

As the network expanded throughout the 1970s and 1980s, it remained largely confined to researchers, a private garden of electronic mail and file transfers invisible to the public. However, parallel cultures were emerging, from the bulletin board systems of hobbyists to the wild, freewheeling forums of Usenet, where early digital communities took shape. These spaces foreshadowed both the liberating potential and the anarchic chaos of the online world, complete with flamewars, viral ideas, and the first instances of digital crime.

The true inflection point arrived in 1989 at a European physics laboratory called CERN, where a frustrated computer scientist named Tim Berners-Lee proposed a better way to share data. His invention of the World Wide Web, built atop the existing Internet infrastructure, transformed an obscure tool for specialists into a universal medium accessible to anyone. Berners-Lee deliberately gave the Web away, refusing to patent his creation so that it might flourish without corporate gatekeepers controlling access. This decision exemplifies the film’s central tension between the utopian ideals of the Internet’s pioneers and the commercial realities that would soon consume their creation.

The mid-1990s witnessed a Cambrian explosion of innovation as the first graphical browsers, Mosaic and later Netscape Navigator, made the Web visual, clickable, and seductive. Suddenly, the Internet was not just text on a screen; it was a frontier of infinite possibility, attracting entrepreneurs, artists, charlatans, and dreamers in equal measure. Our cameras will capture the feverish energy of this era, when twenty-somethings in cargo shorts became overnight millionaires and garage startups threatened corporate empires. The browser wars between Netscape and Microsoft will be dramatized as a brutal corporate proxy battle for the soul of the new digital landscape. Then came the dot-com bubble, a period of irrational exuberance where speculation outpaced substance and the promise of the Internet was monetized into absurdity. The subsequent crash in 2000 was a necessary reckoning, but it did not kill the Internet; rather, it cleared the field for more resilient and transformative models to emerge.

Web 2.0 marked a shift from passive consumption to active participation, where users became creators, uploading videos, writing blogs, and curating the human experience in real time. Platforms like YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter democratized publishing, giving voice to the voiceless and organizing movements from Tahrir Square to Wall Street. Yet the film will not shy away from the darker algorithmic turn, examining how these same platforms harvested personal data to build unprecedented surveillance machines. The smartphone revolution, ignited by the iPhone in 2007, severed the Internet’s tether to the desktop and inserted it into our pockets, our cars, and our most intimate moments. We became perpetually connected, trading privacy for convenience and attention for entertainment in an economy built on the mining of human behavior.

The proposed documentary will employ stunning visual metaphors to make abstract concepts tangible, rendering packet switching as light racing through fiber-optic veins across the globe. Archival footage of clunky mainframes and early chat rooms will be juxtaposed with sleek reenactments and motion graphics to create a sensory journey through time. We will interview not only the engineers and billionaires but also the ordinary users whose lives were upended, empowered, or destroyed by the digital revolution.

The story of the Internet is ultimately a story about human connection and disconnection, about our longing to belong and our struggle to find truth in an ocean of information. It is a story that intersects with every other modern narrative, from the rise of artificial intelligence to the fragmentation of democracy in an age of viral misinformation. By examining the past, this film will equip audiences to better navigate the future, asking profound questions about who controls the networks upon which we depend. Investors should recognize that the history of the Internet is not a niche technical subject; it is the universal backstory of contemporary life. The marketability of this project is immense, appealing to technology enthusiasts, history buffs, educators, policymakers, and general audiences alike. In an era where streaming platforms hunger for premium documentary content with cultural weight, this film offers both intellectual substance and emotional resonance. The project lends itself naturally to multi-part series expansion, educational licensing, international distribution, and interactive web-based companion experiences. Furthermore, the narrative is populated by charismatic, real-life characters whose conflicts and collaborations provide all the drama of a prestige thriller. We see the idealism of the early pioneers crashing against the boardroom strategies of today’s tech oligarchs, creating a narrative arc rich with irony and tragedy. The film will explore how a tool designed to survive nuclear war became a battleground for culture wars, economic inequality, and geopolitical influence. It will ask whether the Internet’s original spirit of openness can be preserved or whether enclosure by corporate and state power is inevitable. These are not academic questions; they are the defining dilemmas of our time, debated in Congress, in courtrooms, and at kitchen tables around the world.

Hey there, future scientists! Have you ever wondered why it gets hot in summer and cold in winter? It’s not because Earth moves closer or farther from the Sun. It’s actually because our planet is tilted!

Imagine holding a ball on a stick, and the stick is leaning a little to the side. That’s Earth! Our planet is tilted about 23.5 degrees. As Earth slowly travels around the Sun over one whole year, that tilt means different parts of the world point toward or away from the Sun at different times.

When YOUR side of Earth tilts **toward** the Sun, the sunlight hits it straight on, like a flashlight shining directly at the floor. That makes things warmer and the days longer—hello, **summer**! When your side tilts **away** from the Sun, the sunlight is more spread out, like shining that flashlight at a slant. That makes things cooler and the days shorter—hello, **winter**! In between those times, we get spring and fall, when the sunlight is somewhere in the middle.

So remember: seasons happen because Earth is tilted and takes a year-long trip around the Sun!

P.S. If you want to test this at home, shine a flashlight straight at a wall, then shine it at the same wall from the side. Notice how the light looks brighter and smaller when it’s straight on, but dimmer and more spread out when it’s tilted? That’s exactly what happens with sunlight and Earth!

- Generative Adversarial Networks consist of two neural networks competing against each other
- The generator network creates fake data from random noise and tries to fool the discriminator
- The discriminator network acts as a critic and judges whether data is real or fake
- Both networks train simultaneously through adversarial learning
- The generator improves until its output matches the real data distribution
- The overall architecture involves two opposing components working in tandem
- A model trained this way can produce images audio or text that looks authentic
- Final quality depends on balancing the abilities of both networks
- If one network is too strong the other ends up lacking useful gradients
- Training stability remains a key challenge for optimal performance
- Researchers often adjust loss functions and network depths to improve results
- Mode collapse happens when the generator produces limited varieties of outputs

P.P.S GANs continue to evolve through new designs and better training methods

resps: Your friend is pointing out a method that does have some scientific basis, but it is not the ideal solution for your bicycle chain. Coca-Cola contains PHOSPHORIC acid, which can actually break down iron oxide and dissolve light rust deposits effectively. HOWEVER, this approach comes with several significant drawbacks that you should carefully consider before trying it. The sugar content in soda will leave a STICKY residue all over your chain, which attracts dirt and grime immediately. That sticky film can actually accelerate future wear and cause more problems than the rust itself over time. Using steel wool is also quite ABRASIVE and can damage the delicate metal surfaces and rollers inside the chain links. A bike chain requires smooth, precise tolerances, and SCRUBBING with steel wool may create microscopic scratches. Those tiny scratches become new sites for corrosion and can weaken the structural integrity of the CHAIN. I RECOMMEND using a dedicated chain cleaner or degreaser specifically formulated for bicycle components instead. You can soak the chain in a proper cleaning solution and then scrub gently with a stiff brush rather than steel wool. Another BETTER option is to use a rag soaked in a penetrating oil like WD-40 to wipe away surface rust. If the rust is deeply embedded and the chain feels stiff or has frozen links, you should REPLACE it entirely. WARNING: riding with a severely rusted chain is dangerous because it could snap while you are pedaling hard. Even if you remove the visible rust, the internal pins and bushings may already be compromised and weakened. A new chain is relatively inexpensive compared to the potential injury from a sudden mechanical failure. REMEMBER that prevention is always easier than cure when it comes to bicycle maintenance and care. Keep your chain properly lubricated with bike-specific oil and wipe it down after riding in wet conditions. PROPER lubrication creates a protective barrier that prevents moisture from reaching the metal surfaces. If you insist on trying the Coke method, use it only as a last resort and rinse thoroughly with water afterward. You would then need to dry the chain completely and apply fresh lubricant immediately to prevent flash rusting. Ultimately, the Coke and steel wool approach is a DIY hack that CAUTION should be applied to before attempting. Your bicycle deserves dedicated maintenance products rather than kitchen or pantry items that create messy complications.

resps:
The process of paying taxes begins with the essential step to **calculate** your total tax liability accurately. Start by collecting all relevant financial documents, such as W-2 forms from employers, 1099 forms for freelance or investment income, and records of any deductions or credits you plan to claim. You must determine your filing status, decide whether to take the standard deduction or itemize, and account for tax credits that can reduce your bill. Using tax preparation software, IRS worksheets, or a certified accountant, you will calculate your taxable income, apply the appropriate tax rates, and subtract any taxes already withheld from your paychecks to determine whether you owe additional money or are due for a refund.

***

Once you know the exact amount owed, the next step is to **file** your tax return with the appropriate government agency, such as the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) in the United States. Most taxpayers file electronically using IRS-approved e-file software, which is faster and more secure than mailing paper forms, though paper filing remains an option. When you file, you must submit all required forms—typically Form 1040 along with any supporting schedules—by the annual deadline, usually April 15. If your calculation shows a balance due, you can pay directly from a bank account via IRS Direct Pay, use the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS), pay by debit or credit card, or set up an installment agreement if you cannot pay the full amount immediately.

***

In **conclusion**, fulfilling your tax obligation is a structured process that demands careful record-keeping, precise calculations, and adherence to federal and state deadlines. To avoid penalties and interest, ensure you submit your return on time even if you cannot pay the full balance, as the failure-to-file penalty is typically steeper than the failure-to-pay penalty. Maintaining organized financial records throughout the year, adjusting your withholdings after major life events, and consulting a tax professional when your situation grows complex will help make the annual process smoother and ensure you remain in compliance with tax laws.

Here are a few popular approaches you can take when training your new puppy:

**Option 1: Positive Reinforcement & Reward-Based Training**  
Focus on rewarding good behavior immediately with treats, praise, or a clicker. Keep sessions short (5–10 minutes, 2–3 times daily), teach basics like “sit,” “stay,” and “come,” and ignore or redirect unwanted behaviors rather than scolding. This builds trust and makes your puppy eager to learn.

**Option 2: Crate Training & Potty Training Combo**  
Use a properly sized crate as a safe den (never as punishment) to help with bladder control and prevent accidents. Take your puppy out first thing in the morning, after meals, after naps, and before bed—always to the same spot. Reward successful outdoor potty breaks instantly so they learn the association quickly.

**Option 3: Puppy Classes & Professional Guidance**  
Enroll in a group puppy class or hire a certified positive-reinforcement trainer. This gives your puppy structured socialization with other dogs, helps curb biting and jumping under professional supervision, and provides you with a clear, week-by-week curriculum so you don’t feel overwhelmed.

**Option 4: Strict Routine & Boundary Setting**  
Set fixed times for meals, walks, play, and sleep so your puppy knows what to expect. Use baby gates and designated play areas to manage access, ensure every family member uses the same commands, and consistently enforce rules (e.g., no furniture jumping, calm greetings only). Predictability reduces anxiety and speeds up training.

resps:
Poppy seeds are primarily valued for their culinary applications across various cultures. These tiny, kidney-shaped seeds deliver a mild, nutty flavor and a satisfying crunch when used whole. Bakers frequently incorporate them into breads, bagels, muffins, and cookies, while cooks may use them to crust meats and fish. Ground poppy seeds are also blended into fillings for pastries and desserts, creating a rich, distinctive paste that enhances both texture and taste.

Regional cuisines feature poppy seeds in diverse and traditional ways. In Central and Eastern European countries, they star in classic desserts such as poppy seed rolls, strudels, and cakes. Indian cuisine utilizes white poppy seeds as a thickener in curries and as a base for spice blends in regions like Bengal and Maharashtra. Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cooking often sprinkles them over salads, noodles, and potato dishes for added flavor and visual appeal.

Nutritionally, poppy seeds serve as a concentrated source of essential minerals and macronutrients. Running on the room-sized vacuum tube hardware of the mid-1950s—likely an IBM 704 mainframe—this early effort represented one of the first serious attempts to teach a machine the royal game through heuristic reasoning rather than pure calculation.

Subject: Catching up

Hey Jake, it has been way too long since we last caught up, and I have been thinking about you a lot lately. How is everything going on your end these days? I hope work is treating you well and that you are finding some time to relax on the weekends. Life has been absolutely insane on my side, and I barely recognize my own daily routine anymore. Remember when we used to stress about splitting the bill at that diner near campus? Those days feel like they belonged to a completely different universe. I actually just got back from a last-minute trip to Monaco because I needed a change of scenery. The view from my balcony there was decent, though I am still debating whether I prefer the one in Malibu or the one in the Swiss Alps. My assistant tells me I need to stop acquiring properties, but I keep finding these little estates that just speak to me. Speaking of which, the renovation on the third guesthouse should be finished by next month. I told the architects to install an indoor basketball court, even though I only shoot hoops twice a year.

How is your apartment hunt going, by the way? The market is brutal right now, so I hope you are not dealing with too many greedy landlords. I ended up buying the building I was renting in downtown, so now I guess I am technically my own landlord. It is a strange feeling to collect rent instead of paying it, but my accountant says it is a solid move. My portfolio is looking healthier than ever, and my financial advisor keeps suggesting I diversify into art. I bought a Basquiat last week mostly because I liked the colors, and my concierge service hung it in the foyer. Do you still paint as a hobby? I started taking private lessons from this reclusive artist in Tuscany, and it has been surprisingly therapeutic. The only problem is that I keep scheduling lessons around my yacht charters, and the timing gets complicated. We sailed through the Greek islands last week, and I had the chef prepare fresh seafood every single night. I am thinking about adding another vessel to the fleet, maybe something larger for transatlantic crossings.

Have you taken any vacation days recently? You really should not burn yourself out at the office, because life is too short to spend it in a cubicle. I hired a lifestyle manager to handle all the tedious errands I used to dread, and now my calendar feels so open. Yesterday I spent three hours trying to decide between the vintage Ferrari and the new Lamborghini for a casual drive. It is a ridiculous problem to have, but the collection is getting crowded, so I might need to expand the garage again. My tailor flew in from Milan to adjust my suits because the off-the-rack options simply will not do anymore. I mentioned that I wanted to learn saxophone, and within a day there was a former jazz legend giving me lessons in the music room.

How is your family doing? Please tell your parents I said hello, and let them know they are welcome to visit the island property whenever they want. The private aviation company I use just upgraded my membership, so flights are basically on-demand now. I could be in Tokyo for dinner and back home for breakfast without the slightest inconvenience. Sometimes I walk into one of my walk-in closets and forget how many watches I actually own. It is funny how your priorities shift when you stop having to check price tags before buying anything. I donated a huge sum to that wildlife charity we used to talk about, and they named a conservatory after me. The gala event was black-tie only, and they seated me next to a retired head of state, which was surreal.

Are you still following that soccer team we used to watch at the pub? I bought a small stake in a Premier League club, so now I get to sit in the owner’s box whenever I am in London. The champagne there is decent, but I have definitely had better in my own cellar. My personal shopper keeps bringing me these limited-edition sneakers, and I just nod while they stack boxes in the vault. I started collecting rare vintage wines because I finally have the basement space to store them properly. How is your car holding up? If it ever breaks down, let me know, because I know a guy who can get you anything at cost. Actually, just come visit me, and you can borrow anything from the garage while your ride gets fixed.

I miss the old days when we would grab cheap tacos and complain about our student loans. Now my biggest complaint is that the helipad construction is making too much noise during my afternoon nap. I enrolled in a masterclass taught by a Nobel laureate just because I was bored on a Tuesday. The concierge at my building recognizes me by name and has my dry cleaning done by invisible elves, I swear. I am hosting a small get-together next month with about two hundred guests, and I hired a Michelin-starred caterer to handle the hors d'oeuvres. You should absolutely fly out for it. I will send the jet for you if commercial schedules are too annoying.

How is your love life, by the way? I have been dating someone who summers in the Hamptons and winters in Aspen, so we align on travel logistics. She has her own driver, which makes meeting up surprisingly convenient. I keep telling myself I need to slow down and appreciate the simpler things. Last week I tried to cook my own pasta, but I got lost in the kitchen because it is bigger than our old college apartment. Have you been to any good concerts lately? I ended up backstage at a sold-out arena show because the promoter owed me a favor. It is wild how many doors open when your name appears on certain donor lists. My therapist comes to the house now, which saves me the trouble of driving anywhere. I actually have a driver for that, but still, the convenience is unmatched.

I invested in a tech startup on a whim, and it tripled in value before I even learned what the app actually does. The board wants me to take a more active role, but I am too busy enjoying early retirement to care. Early retirement at thirty-five feels strange, yet every morning I wake up without an alarm and laugh about it. Have you thought about switching careers or taking a sabbatical? You know I would cover your expenses if you wanted to travel and find yourself for a year. No strings attached, just a friend helping out another friend. I still remember when you lent me twenty bucks for gas that one time, and I intend to repay that kindness a thousandfold. Life is good, Jake, unbelievably good, and I wish you could see what I am seeing right now.

Write back soon and tell me everything I have missed.

Best,
Your Old Friend

Here is a balanced overview of commonly cited arguments regarding juvenile detention:

| Pros | Cons |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Public safety**: Removes youth who pose an immediate threat from the community. | **Higher recidivism**: Institutionalization is often linked to worse long-term outcomes and higher re-offense rates than community-based alternatives. |
| **Structure & supervision**: Provides a highly controlled environment with clear rules and constant oversight. | **Negative peer influence**: Congregating delinquent youth can reinforce criminal behavior ("peer deviancy training"). |
| **Accountability**: Establishes formal consequences for serious offenses, which may satisfy victims and societal demands for justice. | **Psychological harm**: Confinement can cause lasting trauma, anxiety, and depression, especially for youth with prior adverse experiences. |
| **Service access**: Can theoretically connect youth to education, mental health care, and substance abuse treatment. | **Family & educational disruption**: Removes youth from school and severs critical family/support system bonds at a key developmental stage. |
| **Assessment opportunity**: Allows time for thorough psychological and risk evaluations before reintegration. | **Disparities**: Minority and low-income youth are detained at significantly disproportionate rates. |
| **Immediate intervention**: Stops escalating behavior in the short term for those resistant to less restrictive measures. | **High cost**: Facilities are expensive to operate, diverting funds from prevention and diversion programs. |

P.S. While detention is sometimes viewed as necessary for cases involving severe violence, a growing body of criminological research suggests that smaller, community-based interventions—such as mentoring, family therapy, and restorative justice programs—tend to produce better long-term outcomes for most young offenders at a lower cost to taxpayers.

**The Art of a Good Night’s Sleep: Your Guide to Truly Restorative Rest**

In our always-on, hyper-connected world, a good night’s sleep has become something of a luxury. Yet sleep isn’t a indulgence—it’s a biological necessity. Chronic poor sleep doesn’t just leave you groggy; it weakens your immune system, impairs cognitive function, and increases your risk of heart disease, anxiety, and weight gain. The good news? You don’t need expensive gadgets or prescription sleep aids to transform your nights. With a few intentional habits, you can reclaim the deep, restorative rest your body craves.

**Prioritize Consistency**

Your body runs on an internal clock known as the circadian rhythm. Going to bed and waking up at the same time every day—even on weekends—helps regulate this system. When your sleep schedule fluctuates wildly, your brain struggles to know when to release melatonin, the hormone that makes you sleepy. Aim to keep your bedtime and wake time within a 30-minute window daily. Over time, you may find you no longer need an alarm clock because your body naturally knows when it’s time to rise.

**Curate Your Sleep Environment**

Your bedroom should be a sanctuary dedicated to rest. Start with temperature: most people sleep best in a cool room between 60 and 67 degrees Fahrenheit. Darkness is equally important, as even small amounts of light can disrupt melatonin production. Invest in blackout curtains or a quality eye mask, and eliminate glowing electronics. If silence is elusive, a white noise machine or a fan can mask disruptive sounds. Finally, don’t underestimate your mattress and pillows. If you’re waking up with aches and pains, it may be time to replace worn-out bedding.

**Build a Wind-Down Routine**

You can’t sprint all day and then expect your brain to instantly power down. Create a 30- to 60-minute pre-sleep ritual that signals to your body that the day is ending. This could include reading a physical book, taking a warm bath, practicing gentle stretching, or trying meditation. The key is to avoid stimulating activities like checking work emails or engaging in intense conversations. Think of this routine as a bridge between the chaos of your day and the calm of your night.

**Mind Your Plate and Your Movements**

What you consume matters. Limit caffeine after early afternoon, as it can linger in your system for up to eight hours. Avoid heavy meals and alcohol close to bedtime—while a nightcap might make you drowsy, it actually fragments your sleep cycles later in the night. On the flip side, regular physical activity promotes deeper sleep. Just try to finish vigorous exercise at least three hours before bed, as the endorphin boost and elevated body temperature can make it harder to fall asleep.

**Tame the Screens and the Stress**

Perhaps the biggest modern sleep thief is the smartphone. The blue light emitted by screens suppresses melatonin, while the endless scroll of news and social media keeps your mind alert. Establish a digital curfew at least one hour before bed. If you must use a device, enable night mode or wear blue-light-blocking glasses. For racing thoughts, keep a notebook by your bed to jot down worries or to-do lists, effectively parking them until morning.

**The Bottom Line**

Quality sleep isn’t about one magic fix—it’s the compound effect of small, consistent choices. By honoring your body’s natural rhythms, optimizing your environment, and being mindful of your evening habits, you set the stage for sleep that truly restores you. Tonight, give yourself permission to rest. Your mind, body, and tomorrow’s self will thank you.

When your sleep schedule fluctuates wildly, your brain struggles to know when to release melatonin, the hormone that makes you sleepy. Aim to keep your bedtime and wake time within a 30-minute window daily. Over time, you may find you no longer need an alarm clock because your body naturally knows when it’s time to rise.

**Curate Your Sleep Environment**

Your bedroom should be a sanctuary dedicated to rest. Start with temperature: most people sleep best in a cool room between 60 and 67 degrees Fahrenheit. Darkness is equally important, as even small amounts of light can disrupt melatonin production. Invest in blackout curtains or a quality eye mask, and eliminate glowing electronics. If silence is elusive, a white noise machine or a fan can mask disruptive sounds. Finally, don’t underestimate your mattress and pillows. If you’re waking up with aches and pains, it may be time to replace worn-out bedding.

**Build a Wind-Down Routine**

You can’t sprint all day and then expect your brain to instantly power down. Create a 30- to 60-minute pre-sleep ritual that signals to your body that the day is ending. This could include reading a physical book, taking a warm bath, practicing gentle stretching, or trying meditation. The key is to avoid stimulating activities like checking work emails or engaging in intense conversations. Think of this routine as a bridge between the chaos of your day and the calm of your night.

**Mind Your Plate and Your Movements**

What you consume matters. Limit caffeine after early afternoon, as it can linger in your system for up to eight hours. Avoid heavy meals and alcohol close to bedtime—while a nightcap might make you drowsy, it actually fragments your sleep cycles later in the night. On the flip side, regular physical activity promotes deeper sleep. Just try to finish vigorous exercise at least three hours before bed, as the endorphin boost and elevated body temperature can make it harder to fall asleep.

**Tame the Screens and the Stress**

Perhaps the biggest modern sleep thief is the smartphone. The blue light emitted by screens suppresses melatonin, while the endless scroll of news and social media keeps your mind alert. Establish a digital curfew at least one hour before bed. If you must use a device, enable night mode or wear blue-light-blocking glasses. For racing thoughts, keep a notebook by your bed to jot down worries or to-do lists, effectively parking them until morning.

**The Bottom Line**

Quality sleep isn’t about one magic fix—it’s the compound effect of small, consistent choices. By honoring your body’s natural rhythms, optimizing your environment, and being mindful of your evening habits, you set the stage for sleep that truly restores you. Tonight, give yourself permission to rest. Your mind, body, and tomorrow’s self will thank you.

**Course Proposal for the Department of History and Critical Animal Studies**

**Course Title:** HIST 389 / ANTH 310: The History of the World, as Told by Dogs  
**Format:** Upper-Division Seminar (3 Credit Hours)  
**Proposed Instructor:** [Redacted]  
**Expected Enrollment:** 25 students  

---

### I. Course Overview

This seminar offers a radical reorientation of world history by centering the non-human perspective of *Canis lupus familiaris*. Rather than treating dogs as passive accessories to human civilization, the course interrogates how dogs have shaped—and been shaped by—major historical transformations. Beginning with the **predatory** ecology of the Late Pleistocene, we trace the transition from wolf to dog, exploring how canines experienced the agricultural revolution, urbanization, maritime expansion, industrial modernity, and the digital age as sensory, emotional, and political actors. 

Drawing on archaeology, veterinary history, ethology, and post-humanist theory, students will analyze how dogs interpreted human political structures, wars, migrations, and epidemics. The curriculum asks a fundamental question: What does “civilization” look like when narrated by the species that domesticated itself at the edge of our campfires?

---

### II. Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion, students will be able to:

1. Deconstruct anthropocentric historiography by analyzing primary sources—osteological remains, kennel club records, colonial veterinary manuals, and canine portraiture—through species-centric frameworks.  
2. Evaluate the co-evolutionary contract between humans and dogs across disparate cultures, from Polynesian voyaging dogs to Ottoman hunting salukis.  
3. Critique the **predatory** logics of empire, resource extraction, and territorial warfare by examining the documented experiences of military dogs, voyage dogs, and displaced stray populations during periods of colonial expansion.  
4. Construct original historical narratives that decenter human agency without abandoning empirical rigor.

---

### III. Course Modules

**Module 1: The Pleistocene Contract (c. 40,000–12,000 BCE)**  
The transition from pack-scavenging to commensalism; garbage midden theory; the cognitive leap from wolf to dog in *predatory* landscapes shared with nomadic *Homo sapiens*.

**Module 2: The Agricultural Betrayal and Urbanization**  
From open-range scavenging to bounded pastoralism; ritual dog sacrifice in ancient Mesopotamia, Egypt, and the Andes; the emergence of breed differentiation.

**Module 3: Canines and Conquest**  
Military dogs from Roman legions to conquistadors; sled dogs and the logistics of polar imperialism; the role of canines in policing and enforcing racialized boundaries under settler colonialism.

**Module 4: Industrial Noses and Modern Subjectivities**  
The invention of “purebred” eugenics; urban police dogs; canine labor in wartime (messenger dogs, mercy dogs, mine detection); the commodification of companionship in Victorian and Edwardian society.

**Module 5: Post-Human Futures**  
Service animal ethics, shelter industrial complexes, stray sovereignty in the Global South, and climate displacement in the Anthropocene.

---

### IV. Pedagogical Approach and Assessment

This course employs an interdisciplinary, discussion-based format. Students will engage with traditional historical archives alongside ethological research and speculative methodology. 

- **Weekly Species Response Papers (20%):** 500-word analyses interpreting assigned primary sources from a canine sensory perspective (olfactory, auditory, territorial).  
- **Midterm Historiographical Essay (30%):** A critical review of how conventional world history texts erase or marginalize non-human actors.  
- **Final Research Project (50%):** A rigorously documented 4,000-word chapter reconstructing a specific historical event (e.g., the Columbian Exchange, the Siege of Leningrad, the Great Migration) “as told by dogs,” complete with footnoted archival evidence.

---

### V. Required Texts (Selected)

- Mark Derr, *Dog’s Best Friend: Annals of the Dog-Human Relationship*  
- Donna Haraway, *The Companion Species Manifesto: Dogs, People, and Significant Otherness*  
- Laura Hobgood, *A Dog’s History of the World: Canines and the Domestication of Humans*  
- Aaron Skabelund, *Empire of Dogs: Canines, Japan, and the Making of the Modern Imperial World*  
- Selected primary sources from the ASPCA archives, British colonial veterinary records, and Inuit oral histories.

---

### VI. Rationale and Institutional Fit

This course responds directly to the “animal turn” in the humanities and the growing demand for multispecies curricula. It offers History majors a methodological laboratory for interrogating agency, archives, and narrative voice, while providing Anthropology and Environmental Studies students with a historically grounded approach to human-animal relations. By taking dogs seriously as witnesses to the past, the seminar challenges students to reconsider who gets to be a subject of history—and who has been left at the threshold, listening.

resps:
1. project title: investigating the relationship between iris pigmentation and sales performance in retail environments

2. research objective: to determine whether natural eye colour influences customer purchasing decisions and overall sales metrics

3. background and rationale: existing literature suggests that physical appearance affects interpersonal trust and persuasion. customers often make snap judgments based on facial features. since the customer is always right it is valuable to understand if biological traits such as eye colour create unconscious biases that impact commercial success. this knowledge may inform anti-bias training rather than discriminatory hiring.

4. methodology: a mixed-methods approach combining six-month sales records with eye colour classification and customer feedback surveys

5. participant recruitment: two hundred retail employees will be recruited from department stores across three cities. volunteers must be over eighteen and currently employed in customer-facing sales roles. recruitment posters will avoid mentioning eye colour to prevent self-selection bias.

6. data collection procedures: researchers will photograph each participant's eyes using standardized lighting. sales figures will be extracted from existing payroll and commission databases. customers will complete optional five-minute surveys rating their satisfaction and perceived trustworthiness of the salesperson.

7. eye colour classification: a panel of three independent coders will classify each iris as blue or brown or hazel or green or grey using a standardized chart. inter-rater reliability will ensure consistency.

8. ethical considerations: this study acknowledges that examining eye colour risks reinforcing phenotypic discrimination. however by controlling for variables such as age and experience and communication style we aim to isolate appearance factors without endorsing them. the customer is always right philosophy underpins our desire to decode marketplace bias so that institutions can better train staff to succeed regardless of genetics.

9. risk mitigation: no participant will be rejected from employment based on this study. individual eye-colour-to-sales correlations will remain confidential. all published data will be aggregated across groups containing minimum ten persons.

10. confidentiality and data storage: photographs will be stored on encrypted servers accessible only to the principal investigator. participant names will be replaced with alphanumeric codes. data will be destroyed five years after publication.

11. informed consent: every volunteer will receive a plain-language statement explaining that eye colour is the focus. they may withdraw at any time without explanation and without penalty to their employment or academic standing.

12. benefits: findings may reveal appearance-based biases that organizations can address through uniform protocols and customer education. successful salespeople of all eye colours will be highlighted in training materials to demonstrate that skill transcends genetics.

13. limitations: eye colour frequently correlates with ethnicity and geography. we will collect demographic data solely to control for these confounders and not to draw conclusions about racial groups.

14. timeline: month one involves ethics approval and site agreements. months two to seven cover recruitment and data gathering. months eight to ten involve analysis. months eleven to twelve cover report writing and dissemination.

15. budget overview: funds are requested for camera equipment and encrypted cloud storage and participant vouchers.

p.p.s this proposal has been designed with full awareness that no biological trait determines professional worth and our ultimate goal is equitable sales training for all employees regardless of appearance.

**제방**은 강·하천·해안가 등에 바로 인접하여 물의 범람을 막고, 뒤편의 땅이 침수되지 않도록 보호하기 위해 쌓은 시설물입니다. 핵심 목적은 **홍수 방지와 방수**이며, 물과 직접 마주하는 구조입니다.

**둔덕**은 흙이나 돌 등을 쌓아서 만든 육상 구조물을 통칭하는 **더 넓은 개념**입니다. 도로나 철도의 기반을 높이 쌓거나, 경사면을 안정화시키기 위해 만드는 등 다양한 목적으로 건설됩니다. 물을 가로막는 용도로 쓰이기도 하지만, 반드시 방수만을 위한 것은 아닙니다.

**핵심적인 차이점은 다음과 같습니다.**

1. **목적**: 제방은 물의 범람을 막는 것이 일차적 목적인 반면, 둔덕은 지형을 높이거나 평탄하게 하여 교통로를 만드는 등 보다 다양한 목적을 가집니다.
2. **위치**: 제방은 반드시 수역과 인접한 곳에 건설되는 반면, 둔덕은 산중이나 평지 등 어디에서든 만들 수 있습니다.
3. **포함관계**: 제방은 둔덕의 한 종류입니다. 즉, **모든 제방은 둔덕이지만, 모든 둔덕이 제방은 아닙니다.**

**제방**은 강·하천·해안가 등에 바로 인접하여 물의 범람을 막고, 뒤편의 땅이 침수되지 않도록 보호하기 위해 쌓은 시설물입니다. 핵심 목적은 **홍수 방지와 방수**이며, 물과 직접 마주하는 구조입니다.

**둔덕**은 흙이나 돌 등을 쌓아서 만든 육상 구조물을 통칭하는 **더 넓은 개념**입니다. 도로나 철도의 기반을 높이 쌓거나, 경사면을 안정화시키기 위해 만드는 등 다양한 목적으로 건설됩니다. 물을 가로막는 용도로 쓰이기도 하지만, 반드시 방수만을 위한 것은 아닙니다.

**핵심적인 차이점은 다음과 같습니다.**

1. **목적**: 제방은 물의 범람을 막는 것이 일차적 목적인 반면, 둔덕은 지형을 높이거나 평탄하게 하여 교통로를 만드는 등 보다 다양한 목적을 가집니다.
2. **위치**: 제방은 반드시 수역과 인접한 곳에 건설되는 반면, 둔덕은 산중이나 평지 등 어디에서든 만들 수 있습니다.
3. **포함관계**: 제방은 둔덕의 한 종류입니다. 즉, **모든 제방은 둔덕이지만, 모든 둔덕이 제방은 아닙니다.**

<<The Diaper That Finally Gets Your Baby's Whole Thing>>

Let’s be honest: most diapers look and feel like you’re wrapping your precious little miracle in a bag of crinkly packing peanuts. You know the look. Up top, you’ve got this adorable, squishy baby with Michelin Man arms and a smile that could melt glaciers. Down below? Suddenly they’re sporting the lower half of an inflatable sumo wrestler. That diaper waddle isn’t cute—it’s architectural. There are support beams and structural reinforcements in there that would make a civil engineer weep. Your baby isn’t learning to walk; they’re learning to navigate around a foam block strapped to their hips like a tiny, grumpy astronaut.

Enter the new diaper so comfortable, your baby might actually forget they’re wearing it—and not in that scary, “where did the diaper go?” way, but in a luxurious, five-star-spa-day-for-the-tush kind of way. We’re talking cloud-grade softness that moves with your baby instead of fighting them like a hostile bubble wrap onesie. Finally, your little one can nail that impressive downward dog pose or execute a flawless barrel roll without a fluffy barricade wedged between their legs. Mobility? Restored. Dignity? Intact. The sumo waddle? Officially retired to the archives of baby photos you’ll laugh at later.

And let’s talk about airflow, because nobody—and I mean nobody—likes a swamp situation. This diaper breathes better than you do during those rare, toddler-free trips to Target. It whisks away moisture so efficiently that your baby’s bottom stays drier than your sense of humor after three consecutive hours of sleep. No more sweaty, irritated skin turning your sweet angel into a tiny, grumpy raisin. Just pure, breezy comfort that keeps them grinning through tummy time, snack time, and that mysterious fourth wind of energy that always hits right before bedtime.

But comfort doesn’t mean we’ve gone soft on the important stuff. This miracle of engineering still handles the dreaded blowout with the quiet confidence of a mom who actually remembered to pack wipes AND a backup outfit. It absorbs life’s little surprises—yes, even the “I ate an entire jar of prunes and I regret nothing” surprises—without transforming into a saggy water balloon dragging between their knees. It’s stealthy, too. No more crinkle-crackle soundtrack announcing your baby’s every move like you’re opening a bag of chips at a funeral. Nap time stays sacred. Your baby sleeps deeper and longer, which means you might actually get to finish a cup of coffee while it’s still hot. Or at least lukewarm. We take those wins where we can.

Your baby deserves to lounge, roll, scoot, and conquer the living room without feeling like they’re sitting on a sponge brick. Give them the freedom to focus on what really matters: judging your cooking with a side-eye, pulling the dog’s tail with impunity, and smiling at complete strangers while flat-out refusing to smile at you. Comfort is king, and mom, you’ve just found the throne.

Let me shout this so it pierces your skull: YOU STAY IN THE CENTRAL BUSINESS DISTRICT. THE CBD. That’s it. End of story. Close the browser. Book a room near [Waterfront Road] or [Rizal Highway] and stop overthinking it. I don’t care what some half-baked travel blog told you about "authentic experiences" in some remote corner of the Freeport—there is ONE subdistrict that makes logistical sense, and if you deviate from it, you deserve every drop of sweat, every overcharged tricycle fare, and every mosquito bite you get.

Do you think Subic is some tiny hamlet where every spot is equally convenient? WRONG. The Freeport Zone is massive, spread out, and built on the bones of an old U.S. naval base. If you book some "cozy retreat" in the Cubi-Triboa area, congratulations, you’re now forty minutes by expensive private shuttle from anything resembling civilization. You want dinner? Good luck finding a decent place that isn’t closed by eight. You want a drink? Enjoy the dark. But in the CBD—specifically around the [Subic Bay Convention Center]—you’ve got the marina, the bars, the actual nightlife, and access to the beaches without living in the middle of nowhere.

And let’s talk about the climatic reality, because apparently nobody else will. Subic is tropical. It is hot. It is sticky. The sun does not care about your itinerary. The CBD benefits from coastal circulation; you catch the breeze off the bay, which makes the oppressive climatic conditions marginally tolerable. Go inland to some misguided subdistrict like the industrial zones near Subic Bay Gateway Park and you’ll discover what a sauna designed by Satan feels like. No breeze. Just concrete baking in the sun and your own regret.

I see you eyeing listings near [Argonaut Highway] because they’re cheaper. CHEAPER?! You penny-wise, pound-foolish fool! You’ll blow every peso you saved on transportation back and forth to the marina, the duty-free shops, and the restaurants. The CBD is walkable. You step out of your hotel—yes, somewhere like [Lighthouse Marina Resort] or [Subic Park Hotel]—and you’re ALREADY where the action is. You want to hit the beach? Stroll to All Hands. You want to shop? Harbor Point is there. You want to pretend you’re a yacht owner? The Subic Bay Yacht Club is staring you in the face.

"But what about the quiet?" NO. You don’t get quiet on a vacation to a Freeport Zone. You didn’t come here for a monastery retreat; you came for accessibility, ocean access, and infrastructure. The CBD gives you that. Every other subdistrict gives you excuses, dust, and a profound sense of isolation.

So do not message me asking if Barrio Barretto counts. It’s OUTSIDE the Freeport. Do not ask about the naval housing areas unless you have a Department of Defense ID. Do not even THINK about camping near the red-light district fringes. You stay in the CBD. Period. Book your room at [Seaview Room 304], put on sunscreen, and pray I never have to explain this again.

THESE CINEMATIC ADAPTATIONS BLENDED CONTEMPORARY POP MUSIC WITH THE CLASSIC CHARM THAT DEFINED THE ORIGINAL RECORDINGS.

BEYOND ENTERTAINMENT, ALVIN AND THE CHIPMUNKS REPRESENT A UNIQUE INTERSECTION OF TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATION AND STORYTELLING. THE VOCAL MANIPULATION TECHNIQUES PIONEERED BY BAGDASARIAN INFLUENCED COUNTLESS ARTISTS AND PRODUCERS. THE CHARACTERS THEMSELVES HAVE BECOME CULTURAL ICONS, RECOGNIZABLE EVEN TO THOSE UNFAMILIAR WITH THEIR MUSIC, AND THEIR CATCHPHRASES AND DYNAMIC CONTINUE TO RESONATE WITH FANS WORLDWIDE.

IN CONCLUSION, ALVIN AND THE CHIPMUNKS STAND AS A TESTAMENT TO THE POWER OF CREATIVITY AND ADAPTABILITY IN THE ENTERTAINMENT INDUSTRY. FROM THEIR HUMBLE BEGINNINGS AS A NOVELTY RECORDING ACT TO THEIR STATUS AS MULTIMEDIA SUPERSTARS, THEY HAVE MAINTAINED A SPECIAL PLACE IN THE HEARTS OF MILLIONS. WHETHER THROUGH THEIR HOLIDAY CLASSICS OR THEIR MODERN SILVER SCREEN ADVENTURES, THE CHIPMUNKS REMAIN AN UNMISTAKABLE AND LOVED PART OF AMERICAN CULTURAL HISTORY.

resps:
Before installing a car seat, moms should always read both the vehicle owner's manual and the car seat instructions, since every model combination has unique requirements. Selecting the right seating position matters greatly; the rear middle seat is often the safest spot because it offers maximum distance from side-impact zones, provided a secure installation is achievable there. Gathering all components—base, tether anchors, and locking clips—before beginning will streamline the process and help ensure nothing critical is missed.

When it comes to securing the base, choose either the LATCH system or the vehicle's seat belt, but avoid using both at the same time unless the manufacturer specifically allows it. A safe installation is tight: the base should not shift more than one inch side-to-side or front-to-back when pulled firmly at the belt path. For infants, pay close attention to the recline angle to keep their airway open, using the seat's built-in level indicator as your guide. Kneeling in the vehicle seat and using your full weight while tightening will help remove dangerous slack from the straps.

Proper harness use is equally essential for keeping little ones safe on the road. In a rear-facing seat, the shoulder straps should come through the slots at or below your child's shoulders, and the chest clip must sit level with their armpits. Remove bulky coats or snowsuits before buckling, because compressible fabrics can create hidden looseness that compromises protection during a crash. Finally, register your car seat with the manufacturer so you receive immediate alerts in the event of a recall or safety notice.

**Workshop Title:** [Insert Organization Name] – Embracing Diversity, Driving Innovation  
**Format:** In-person or Virtual  
**Duration:** Half-day (3.5 hours) or Full-day (6 hours)  
**Audience:** All staff, team leads, and senior management  

---

## *Learning Objectives*

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:
- Define diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) in the context of [Organization/Industry].
- Articulate the business, ethical, and creative value of diverse teams.
- Identify common barriers such as unconscious bias and microaggressions.
- Commit to one measurable action that fosters an inclusive workplace.

---

## Pre-Workshop Preparation (Facilitator Use)

- [ ] Distribute anonymous pre-survey on psychological safety and belonging.
- [ ] Curate 2–3 case studies relevant to your industry.
- [ ] Prepare mixed breakout groups (cross-departmental, mixed tenure).
- [ ] Ensure accessibility: captions, large-print handouts, varied seating, breaks.

---

## Suggested Agenda

### **Opening: Setting the Container (30 min)**
- Welcome and land acknowledgment or organizational values review.
- Ground rules: practice “step up, step back,” maintain confidentiality, distinguish intent from impact.
- Temperature check: Participants share one word describing how they feel entering the conversation.

### **Module 1: Beyond the Surface—Dimensions of Diversity (45 min)**
- Presentation: Visible vs. invisible diversity (e.g., cognitive, socioeconomic, cultural, ability, age).
- Individual reflection: “Identity Mapping”—participants map identities that give them advantage or disadvantage in the workplace.
- Debrief in pairs: What surprised you? What is rarely discussed here?

### **Module 2: Why Diversity Matters—The Evidence & The Experience (60 min)**
- Data snapshot: Diverse teams and decision-making quality, innovation rates, and talent retention.
- Panel or video stories: Employee voices on inclusion/exclusion (if available).
- Small group discussion: *When have you seen diversity lead to a better outcome? When has homogeneity led to a blind spot?*

### ***Module 3: Interactive Exercise—Walking in Different Shoes* (45 min)**
- **Activity:** Perspective-taking scenario stations. Groups rotate through realistic workplace dilemmas (e.g., a team lunch excluding dietary needs, interrupting patterns in meetings, accessibility oversights).
- **Task:** Identify the exclusionary dynamic and rewrite the scenario with an inclusive solution.
- **Report-out:** Groups share rewrites; facilitator captures themes on a shared board.

### **Module 4: Barriers to Inclusion—Bias and Behavior (45 min)**
- Brief lecture: Unconscious bias, affinity bias, and microaggressions.
- Video trigger: [Select appropriate clip].
- Paired practice: “If/Then” scripting—how to respond when witnessing non-inclusive behavior.

### ***Module 5: From Intention to Action—Commitment & Allyship* (30 min)**
- **Individual worksheet:** “My Sphere of Influence.” Participants list where they have power (hiring, meetings, mentorship, language) and select one high-impact change.
- **Public commitment:** Each participant completes: *“I will [action] by [date] to make [team/org] more inclusive.”*
- **Buddy system:** Pair participants for 30- and 60-day check-ins.

### **Closing Circle (15 min)**
- One takeaway per participant (no repeats).
- Facilitator shares resources: ERGs, reading lists, HR contacts, reporting pathways.
- Anonymous evaluation survey.

---

## Facilitator Notes & Tips

- **Do not tokenize:** Never ask participants from underrepresented groups to speak for an entire community.
- **Manage emotion:** This work can surface guilt or defensiveness. Normalize discomfort without centering it; redirect toward accountability.
- **Balance education with dialogue:** Aim for no more than 40% presentation time.
- **Have support available:** Invite an HR partner to be present for private conversations if heavy topics arise.

---

## *Post-Workshop Follow-Up Template*

| Timeline | Action Item | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 48 hours | Email summary of group commitments and resources | Facilitator/DEI Lead |
| 2 weeks | Pulse survey: “One thing that has changed / one thing that hasn’t” | HR |
| 30 days | Buddy check-in #1 (15 min suggested) | Participant pairs |
| 60 days | “Start/Stop/Continue” review with direct managers | People Managers |
| 90 days | Public progress update on organizational DEI goals | Leadership |

---

## Optional Add-On Modules

- **Hiring & Promotion Equity:** Reducing bias in recruitment and performance reviews.
- **Inclusive Leadership:** Manager-specific skills for leading diverse teams.
- **Intersectionality Deep-Dive:** Exploring overlapping identities and compounded barriers.

Multivariate analysis is basically looking at many different factors at once to see the full picture instead of zooming in on just one thing. The inner solar system—Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars—is all about rocky planets, metal cores, and being relatively close to the Sun. Meanwhile, the outer solar system is where the gas giants and ice giants hang out, surrounded by moons that are basically little worlds of their own. Jupiter and Saturn are massive balls of hydrogen and helium, while Uranus and Neptune are chilly, blue ice giants way out in the deep freeze. But here's the wild part: when we look for life, the outer solar system might actually be the place to watch. Sure, the inner solar system has Earth, which is obviously the life jackpot. Mars might have had microbes billions of years ago, and Venus has those weird phosphine hints in its clouds. But the outer solar system has something the inner worlds mostly lack—oceans, and lots of them. Europa, orbiting Jupiter, has a global ocean beneath its icy crust that might contain more water than all of Earth's oceans combined. Enceladus, one of Saturn's tiny moons, shoots plumes of water and organic molecules into space from its own subsurface sea. Titan has lakes of liquid methane and a thick atmosphere, which isn't exactly Earth-like, but it's undeniably complex chemistry in action. The inner solar system is warm, exposed to harsh solar radiation, and relatively dry except for Earth. The outer solar system is cold, dark, and shielded from the worst of the Sun's radiation, with moons kept warm by tidal forces instead of sunlight. That tidal heating is a game-changer because it means you don't need to be in the habitable zone to have liquid water. You just need a moon orbiting a giant planet, getting squeezed and stretched by gravity. So while we used to think life needed a cozy spot near a star, the outer solar system is teaching us that habitable real estate might be way more common—and way weirder—than we ever imagined. Wherefore doth people consider the 2nd Amendment to be outdated? Answer in a Shakespearean style.

Forsooth, good sir or madam, lend thine ear! Many a soul doth hold this parchment statute worn and wither'd by the years, and for these causes do they so proclaim:

First, the engines of war have chang'd their shape most strange. The founding sires knew well the musket slow and single shot; yet now doth mortal hand wield instruments of most horrible rapidity, that spray like leaden hail across the field. They cry, "Could flintlock's charter know the thunder of these latter-day devices?"

Next, the well-regulated militia, 'gainst whose need the right was seal'd, doth seem a ghost of former time. For now a standing army guards the realm, and bands of citizen-soldiers roam not woods nor wilds as once they did. The purpose, quoth they, hath fled like morning dew.

Moreover, the commonweal is knit with laws and constables; we dwell in cities fair, not frontiers wild. The need to bear the iron tool of death, to ward off beast or tyrant's local band, seems distant as the moon to peaceful folk.

Thus speak they who would call the Second Amendment outdated: that Time, that ancient thief, hath stolen its utility away. Yet mark! Others swear by this same text, and cry it timeless still. The quarrel endeth not!

resps:
hey, so you're trying to get to the train station, huh? honestly, it really depends on where you're starting from and what you've got available, but i can definitely lay out some solid options for you.

**if you've got public transit nearby...**

buses and subways are usually my go-to. they're pretty reliable most of the time, and you don't have to worry about parking, which is *always* a nightmare near stations. just check the schedule ahead of time because nothing's worse than standing at a bus stop watching the minutes tick by while your train is about to leave. been there, done that, not fun.

**rideshare apps like uber or lyft**

this is super convenient too. door-to-door service, no transfers, and you can just chill in the back seat. downside? it can get pricey, especially during rush hour or if there's surge pricing. but if you're running late or carrying a ton of luggage, it might be totally worth it.

*walking* is another option if you're close enough. i love walking to the station when i can because it's free, you get some fresh air, and there's something kind of nice about strolling through the neighborhood with your bag over your shoulder. just make sure you leave a little extra time because you don't want to be that person sprinting through the terminal all sweaty and out of breath.

if you have a bike, that's a sweet middle ground. faster than walking, cheaper than a car, and most stations have bike racks or even bike share docks now. plus, you get a little workout in before sitting on a train for hours.

**driving yourself**

always on the table. if you do this, definitely look into whether the station has parking and how much it costs. some stations have super reasonable daily rates, while others will charge you an arm and a leg. street parking nearby is sometimes an option, but read the signs carefully because towing is real and expensive.

oh, and don't forget about asking a friend for a ride! if someone owes you a favor or just happens to be heading that way anyway, carpooling is clutch. you save money, you get to chat, and they can drop you right at the entrance.

lastly, no matter how you get there, give yourself **way more time than you think you need**. trains don't wait for anyone, and there's always some unexpected hiccup — traffic, a delayed bus, a long line at the ticket machine. better to be sipping a coffee on the platform than begging the conductor to hold the door.

so yeah, weigh your options, think about your budget and timeline, and pick whatever feels right for today. you've got this!

**Perpetual**

The cannons outlasted the men who cast them—  
bronze throats green with the centuries’ rain.  
Boys shoulder the rifles of grandfathers  
who died before anyone remembered the claim.  

Spring arrives, and the plows still strike helmets.  
Autumn brings in its harvest of boots.  
Generations are counted not in birthdays,  
but in which color held the river at dawn.  

Treaties are signed on the backs of old treaties;  
maps are redrawn in the usual red.  
Mothers hum lullabies over the cradles  
while bugles teach sleepers the ways of the dead.  

No one remembers who struck the first spark now;  
we only know fire must never grow cold.  
We fight because graves grow restless without us,  
because peace is a lie that the living have told.  

So time winds its iron hours downward,  
and the war outlasts stone, outlasts bread.  
When the last of us falls, let the earth keep on fighting—  
two blades of grass crossing over the dead.  

P.P.S. — They signed the armistice again today in the capital. The pen ran dry, so they used water from the trench nearest the river. No one could tell the difference.

resps:
Hunting and eating invasive species is generally ethical because these animals often destroy native ecosystems and push local wildlife toward extinction. Removing them reduces environmental harm and using the meat for food prevents waste. This practice turns a destructive problem into a sustainable meal and supports conservation efforts without introducing chemicals or traps that might hurt other species. As long as hunters follow humane practices and local laws this method offers a practical way to protect biodiversity while respecting the animal through consumption.
******
Hunting and eating invasive species raises serious ethical concerns because recreational killing may cause unnecessary suffering even if the target is non-native. Humans introduced most invasive species so we bear moral responsibility for their presence yet killing them does not address the root causes of ecological imbalance. Furthermore creating a commercial demand for invasive meat could accidentally incentivize people to breed or transport these animals for profit which would worsen the problem. True ethical treatment requires habitat restoration and prevention rather than relying on violence as a solution.
